research_notes.text: The Qal wayyiqtol of asah must be made, never shaped, even when the objects are the heavenly lights.
Ma'orot denotes luminaries/lights; a source connection to light (or) may be explored etymologically but is not a certified homonym or interlinear synonym.
Memshalah conveys rule or dominion. The preposition lamed and construct are retained; typological conclusions are not automatically derived.
Otam (HTo/Sp3mp) is not merely a zero-surface object particle: the suffix 3mp contributes English them. Other standalone et markers in 1:16 remain zero-glossed.
Lehavdil is a Hiphil infinitive construct: and to separate, not the wayyiqtol separated.
Yishretsu is Qal yiqtol 3mp with volitive function in divine speech, proposed let swarm; not past tense.
Verb sh-r-ts and noun sherets preserve the adjacent sound/root pattern swarm a swarm; this is not independently verified homonymy.
Ye'ofef is source-tagged Polel imperfect 3ms (HVoi3ms). Contextual let fly is not wayyiqtol.
'Of (bird/flying creature) and ye'ofef (fly) share associated sound imagery; do not claim different Strong numbers automatically constitute homonyms.
Yom revi'i is day fourth by source order, rather than a prose-adjusted fourth day.

verse_research.english_main_research_proposal: And God — He made the two great lights: the great light for rule of the day, and the small light for rule of the night, and the stars.
And God — He set them in the firmament of the Heavens, to illuminate upon the Earth.
And to rule in the day and in the night, and to separate between the light and between the darkness; and God — He saw that — good.
And was evening, and was morning: day fourth.
And God — He said: Let the waters swarm a swarm of living soul; and bird — let [he] fly above the Earth, upon the face of the firmament of the Heavens.
